title: Lemar Marie Brown (board director · former Texas A&M professor) on hearing the keynote — 'It was a full-circle moment for me'
summary: A board director who taught the Lean Startup method to Executive MBA students at Texas A&M describes watching its author turn to the other end of the problem: how good corporate governance can produce unintended bad consequences.
blockquote: Eric Ries spoke about his new book, Incorruptible: Why Good Companies Go Bad and How Great Companies Stay Great. It was a full-circle moment for me. When I was a professor at Texas A&M, we taught his Lean Startup method to our Executive MBA students. Hearing him now turn to how “good” corporate governance can have unintended “bad”  consequences.
attribution_title: Board Director, NACD.DC · former professor, Texas A&M
